Subject: Evaluation metrics runbook and MAP benchmarking scope

Priya — thanks again for the sync today. Per our conversation I took a pass at a focused benchmarking runbook to include directly in the MAP. The goal is to validate that the selected model family meets Acme's production SLOs under a representative workload before the pilot close. High level asks from Acme for the MAP: 1) performance targets; 2) acceptance criteria for concurrency; 3) sample traces and dataset; 4) a cutover/rollback plan.

I attached a working MAP spreadsheet (acme_map_v2.xlsx) with a proposed testing schedule — please confirm the peak concurrency and whether the anonymized traces you mentioned cover both chat and batch embedding flows.

Proposed success criteria (first pass):
- P95 generation latency under 150 ms (tail must be investigable)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) < 400 ms for warmed endpoints
- Sustained throughput of 2,000–2,500 req/s at target concurrency (64 concurrent sessions)
- No request error rate > 0.5% during steady-state runs

Planned tests (details to follow from Karthik):
- Cold start TTFT matrix across instance types
- Steady-state concurrency ramp (10 -> 64) with 15-minute plateaus
- KV/prefix cache effectiveness check (repeat runs)
- Quantization variant comparison (int8 vs fp16) for cost/perf tradeoffs

Next steps: can you confirm the sample traces and desired run window (we normally run longer tests overnight to avoid noisy infra)? Once confirmed Karthik will drop the test config JSON and we’ll schedule the first run.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for putting this together. Confirming:
- Peak user-facing concurrency: 60–70 concurrent chat sessions during peak; embeddings batch jobs are separate (target 1.2k embeddings/s at peak).
- We will provide an anonymized 48-hour trace that includes chat session lengths and embedding batch timings. Infra will drop the trace into the shared Drive folder by EOD 7/31.
- Acceptance: we'd expect P95 latency similar to your proposed numbers, but we need a TTFT budget of <= 350 ms for priority customers (we can tolerate 400 ms for non-priority).

Can you add a note in the MAP that priority vs non-priority profiles will be run as separate test-cases? Also, include a billing estimate for int8 vs fp16 configurations — John from CloudBroker will help with the cost baseline.

Subject: Re: Evaluation metrics runbook and MAP benchmarking scope — test config

Folks — dropping the technical test plan and acceptance criteria below (I’ll push test_config.json to the Drive). Please review and flag anything we can't run in our hosted environment.

Test harness: JMeter + custom runner (redwood-bench v1.8). Tests will be run against a dedicated pool (isolated GPUs) to avoid noisy neighbors. Each run will record: latency histograms (p50/p90/p95/p99), TTFT, throughput, CPU/GPU utilization, and request error codes.

Workload definitions:
A) Interactive chat profile (priority):
  - Avg session length: 2.3 turns (50 tokens/turn)
  - QPS per session: 0.4
  - Concurrency target: 64 (range 10 -> 64 ramp)

B) Embeddings batch profile (bulk):
  - Batch size: 128
  - Target throughput: 1,200 embeddings/s sustained
  - Concurrency: 12 parallel batch workers

Success criteria / SLOs (strict):
  - Chat p95 generation latency <= 140 ms
  - Chat TTFT <= 350 ms (priority profile)
  - Embeddings throughput >= 1,200 embeddings/s with <0.5% errors
  - End-to-end SLA pass: 95% of runs meet the above thresholds

Bench variants to run:
 1) fp16 baseline (current default)
 2) int8 quantized (aggressive cost saving)
 3) cached-kv enabled vs disabled

Data & tracing: Acme will provide 48h anonymized traces. We'll also seed a synthetic amplification set if needed to hit sustained QPS. Test run cadence: 3 full runs per variant, median results used for acceptance.

Notes for MAP: include a contingency window (48 hours) for flaky runs and a rollback path in case the fp16->int8 variant shows quality regressions. I’ll attach the test_config.json and a sample JMeter template.

—Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — quick alignment and MAP milestones so we can keep the close on track: 

1) Test window: Redwood will run the benchmark suite starting 2026-08-03 22:00 PDT (overnight) — 3 runs per variant; expected completion 2026-08-04 08:00 PDT.
2) Preliminary results: Redwood to share bench_results_20260801.csv (prelim) by 2026-08-01 EOD for review — this will include p50/p90/p95/p99, TTFT, throughput, and resource utilization. Final validated results to be delivered by 2026-08-05 17:00 PDT.
3) Acceptance gating: Acme to sign-off on priority profile SLOs (chat p95 <= 140ms, TTFT <= 350ms) by 2026-08-06. If thresholds are missed, we’ll schedule an immediate deep-dive and at least one re-run within the contingency window (48 hours).
4) Cost/variant recommendation: Redwood will include an int8 vs fp16 ROI table and a suggested rollout plan (canary on 10% traffic) in the final MAP appendix.
5) Contract close target: 2026-08-12 (subject to sign-off and SOC2 evidence delivery).

Action items:
- Acme Infra: confirm trace upload to Drive (assigned) — status: uploaded
- Priya: confirm priority/non-priority customer list for test labeling — due 2026-08-01
- Karthik: push test_config.json + runner scripts to Drive — done by 2026-08-01
- Marissa: compile preliminary results and share — 2026-08-01 EOD

If all looks good we’ll annotate the MAP sheet with the test cases and acceptance rows and move the MAP to the legal/finance queue.

Marissa
